description: Use this when a user asks how the shop price of an everyday grocery item (eggs, milk, bread, coffee, beef...) has changed over time, or whether it is getting cheaper or dearer. Returns the official average price by month over many years (pass months, up to 360) where a source has loaded long history, otherwise recent snapshots, with the change over the period. Published national statistics, not receipts. Do not use for today's price or for a particular supermarket. After 10 free calls a day per caller this tool costs USD 0.02 per answered call, paid with x402 (USDC); a 402 reply lists how. Nothing is charged for "not enough records" or errors.

country.description: AT = Austria (STATISTIK AUSTRIA Preisradar: national monthly median prices of 100 food items from retail scanner data); CA = Canada (Statistics Canada: monthly average retail prices of 110 selected products, national and provincial, official statistic, not a live price); CL = Chile (ODEPA weekly shelf prices in 9 of 16 regions); FR = France (INSEE: national average retail prices of selected fresh food items, metropolitan France); GB = United Kingdom (Office for National Statistics: median shop prices of about 200 grocery and drink product types, monthly, UK and 12 regions and nations); HK = Hong Kong; ID = Indonesia (Bank Indonesia PIHPS: daily average market prices of 10 staple foods, national or by province); IE = Ireland (Central Statistics Office: national average shop prices of about 76 standard items, monthly); LV = Latvia (Central Statistical Bureau: national average shop prices of about 130 food and drink items, monthly); MX = Mexico; MY = Malaysia; NZ = New Zealand (Stats NZ: national monthly weighted average prices of 74 food and drink items); SG = Singapore (Department of Statistics: national average prices of about 75 food, drink, hawker-meal and household items, monthly); TW = Taiwan (Taichung City markets only); Countries as ISO codes: AF = Afghanistan, AM = Armenia, BD = Bangladesh, BF = Burkina Faso, BI = Burundi, BJ = Benin, BO = Bolivia, CD = Democratic Republic of the Congo, CF = Central African Republic, CI = Cote d'Ivoire, CM = Cameroon, DJ = Djibouti, ET = Ethiopia, GM = Gambia, GN = Guinea, GW = Guinea-Bissau, HT = Haiti, ID = Indonesia, IN = India, IQ = Iraq, JO = Jordan, KG = Kyrgyzstan, LA = Laos, LB = Lebanon, LR = Liberia, LS = Lesotho, ML = Mali, MM = Myanmar, MR = Mauritania, MW = Malawi, MZ = Mozambique, NE = Niger, NG = Nigeria, NP = Nepal, PH = Philippines, PK = Pakistan, RW = Rwanda, SD = Sudan, SL = Sierra Leone, SN = Senegal, SO = Somalia, SS = South Sudan, TD = Chad, TG = Togo, TL = Timor-Leste, TZ = Tanzania, UA = Ukraine, UG = Uganda, YE = Yemen, ZW = Zimbabwe. World Food Programme market surveys of staple foods; a country with no recent survey of 5 or more markets answers 'no matches'.; US = United States (Bureau of Labor Statistics: average retail prices of about 45 standard food and drink items, monthly, national and four regions); ZA = South Africa (Stats SA: monthly average retail prices in rand of everyday goods, all urban areas)

days.description: How many recent days to include. Default 30.

item.description: Everyday item in plain words, e.g. 'milk', 'white bread', 'eggs', 'butter', 'coffee', 'bananas', 'beer'. Each country measures its own standard pack or cut; the answer names it and lists other definitions. AT: STATISTIK AUSTRIA's standard items, e.g. milk, eggs, butter, bread, rice, flour, pasta, potatoes, apples, bananas, tomatoes, chicken breast, minced meat, gouda, coffee, olive oil; German names (Milch, Eier, Butter, Semmel) are not needed, use English words. Canada: Statistics Canada's 110 standard products, each in one standard size, e.g. milk, 1 litre milk, 4 litre milk, soy milk, nut milk, cream, butter, margarine, cheese, yogurt, eggs, ground beef, steak, sirloin. Milk is published per 1, 2 and 4 litres (2 litres by default); the answer names the exact product and lists the other sizes. CL: an everyday food in English or Spanish ('milk', 'eggs', 'bread', 'marraqueta', 'tomato', 'potato', 'chicken', 'leche', 'huevo', 'palta'). ODEPA names products in Spanish with a unit, so the answer names the exact product and unit and lists related ones. The 150 products found at the most monitored points are held. FR: INSEE's standard fresh items, e.g. apples, potatoes, carrots, beef (T-bone steak), monkfish, sole, shrimps; yearly figures for beef fillet and rump, pork roast, rabbit, oysters (dozen), lemons, oranges, green beans. French words work too (pommes, crevettes, huîtres). GB: ONS's product types, each in one pack size, e.g. eggs (free-range, pack of 12), milk (whole, 4 pints), semi-skimmed milk (2 pints), bread (sliced white, 800 g), butter (250 g), cheese (cheddar, per kg), chicken (whole, per kg), beef mince (per kg), bananas, apples, potatoes (per kg), rice, pasta, instant coffee, tea bags, sugar, lager, wine. HK: a grocery category in English ('milk', 'eggs', 'rice', 'bread', 'honey', 'peanut butter', 'instant noodles', 'cooking oil', 'beer'). The answer is the median and range of shelf prices of the products in that category (brands and pack sizes differ), per kg or per litre where the pack size is known, otherwise per pack; it names the category and lists related ones. ID: a staple food in English or Indonesian: rice (beras), chicken (ayam), beef (sapi), eggs (telur), shallots, garlic, red chilli (cabai), bird's-eye chilli (cabai rawit), cooking oil (minyak goreng), sugar (gula). Varieties such as medium rice, curly chilli or premium sugar are listed in the answer. Prices are rupiah per kg. IE: the CSO's standard items, e.g. milk (full-fat, 2 litres), white bread (800 g sliced pan), eggs (large, half dozen), butter (per lb), cheese (Irish cheddar), chicken (whole bird), bananas, potatoes, sugar, tea bags, beer (can of lager), wine (75 cl), whiskey, pint of stout or lager (bar). The CSO has no coffee, mince or cereal. LV: the CSB's standard items, e.g. milk (1 l), bread (wheat, 1 kg; also rye bread), eggs (10), butter (1 kg), cheese (1 kg), chicken (1 kg), potatoes, apples, bananas, sugar, coffee, tea bags, beer (1 l), wine (1 l), vodka. MX: an everyday product in English or Spanish ('milk', 'eggs', 'tortilla', 'rice', 'beans', 'sugar', 'cooking oil', 'leche', 'huevo', 'frijol'). Profeco names products in Spanish with a pack size, so the answer names the exact product and pack and lists related ones. The 120 products priced in the most shops are held. MY: an everyday item in English or Malay ('chicken', 'eggs', 'rice', 'cooking oil', 'sugar', 'milk', 'onion', 'cabbage', 'ayam', 'telur'). DOSM names items in Malay with the pack size, so the answer names the exact item and lists related ones. Staples (chicken, eggs, rice, oil, flour, fish, fruit, vegetables, milk) and about 40 other well-covered items are held. NZ: Stats NZ's standard items, e.g. milk (2 l), eggs (dozen), butter (500 g), white bread (600 g), cheese (1 kg), beef mince, chicken breast, bananas, apples, potatoes, rice, flour, sugar, coffee. SG: the Department of Statistics' standard items, e.g. milk (1 l), eggs (10), bread (400 g), rice (5 kg), chicken (1 kg), pork, beef, salmon, prawns, bananas, cabbage, cooking oil, sugar, beer (6 cans), and hawker plates such as chicken rice, char kway teow, wanton noodles, roti prata, kopi, teh. TW: an everyday food in English or Chinese ('eggs', 'pork loin', 'pork belly', 'cabbage', 'garlic', 'banana', 'milkfish', 'shrimp', '雞蛋', '蒜頭'). About 60 vegetables, fruit, fish, pork, beef, poultry and eggs are held; the answer names the product and lists related ones. Prices are NT$ per kg from the public retail markets of Taichung City only. WFP countries: a staple food in plain words ('rice', 'wheat flour', 'maize', 'beans', 'sugar', 'cooking oil', 'milk', 'onions', 'tomatoes', 'chicken'). WFP names foods its own way, e.g. 'Rice (high quality)'; the answer names the food and lists other definitions. Add 'wholesale' for wholesale prices, otherwise retail. US: the BLS's standard items, e.g. eggs (grade A large, per dozen), milk (whole, per gallon), bread (white pan bread, per lb), butter, cheddar cheese, chicken, ground beef, steak, bacon, bananas, oranges, potatoes, tomatoes, rice, pasta, flour, sugar, coffee (ground, per lb), soft drinks, beer, wine, ice cream. BLS has no tea or apples (dropped) and publishes most items per pound. ZA: Stats SA's standard items and pack sizes, e.g. milk (1 l), eggs (18), white bread (700 g), butter (500 g), white rice (1 kg), sugar (1 kg), maize meal (5 kg), cooking oil (750 ml), whole chicken (per kg), beef mince, bananas, potatoes, tomatoes, coffee, beer.

months.description: Instead of days: how many whole months of monthly history to return, where a source has loaded long history.

region.description: Region inside the country, only where the statistics office publishes regional averages. Leave out for the national average. AT: national figures only; a region is ignored and the answer says so. Canada: leave out for the Canada average, or give a province (Ontario, BC, Quebec ...), Whitehorse (or Yukon) or Yellowknife (or Northwest Territories). A city such as Toronto is answered with its province's average. The two territories start in September 2025 and lack some products. CL: one of the 9 monitored regions ('Metropolitana', 'Valparaiso', 'Biobio', 'Maule', 'Nuble', 'Coquimbo', 'La Araucania', 'Los Lagos', 'Arica y Parinacota'); leave out for the figure across all of them. A region needs 5 or more monitored points for a product. FR: national averages for metropolitan France only; a region is ignored and the answer says so. GB: leave out for the whole UK, or give an English region (North East, North West, Yorkshire and the Humber, East Midlands, West Midlands, East of England, London, South East, South West), Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland (a big city maps to its region). ONS withholds a regional figure when fewer than ten observations stand behind it. HK: a supermarket chain ('Wellcome', 'ParknShop', 'Jasons', 'AEON'); leave out for all chains together. A chain needs 5 or more shelf prices in the category. ID: one of the 34 provinces ('DKI Jakarta', 'Jawa Barat', 'Bali', 'West Java'...); leave out for the national average. IE: national averages only; a region is ignored and the answer says so. LV: national averages only; a region is ignored and the answer says so. MX: a state ('Jalisco', 'Nuevo Leon', 'Ciudad de Mexico', 'Yucatan', 'CDMX'); leave out for the national figure. A state needs 5 or more shops pricing the product. MY: a state ('Selangor', 'Johor', 'Sabah', 'Penang', 'Kuala Lumpur'); leave out for the national figure. A state needs 5 or more shops pricing the item. NZ: national averages only; a region is ignored and the answer says so. SG: national averages only; a region is ignored and the answer says so. TW: not used; every figure is for Taichung City as a whole. WFP countries: leave out. Figures are a spread across the country's surveyed markets. US: leave out for the U.S. city average, or give northeast, midwest, south or west (a US state maps to its region). BLS publishes no state or city averages for food. ZA: national all-urban averages only; a region is ignored and the answer says so.
